text:
The most serious crime is second-degree murder. Firing a gun at a person in a crowded game shows extreme recklessness about human life (depraved-heart malice), and in many jurisdictions it also supports felony murder based on the aggravated battery. I disagree with the team note: criminal negligence and "no malice" don't fit here, because deliberately shooting someone with a gun is not an accident, and malice doesn't require intent to kill. First-degree murder is unlikely because there was no premeditated intent to kill, and in jurisdictions that apply the merger doctrine the felony-murder route may fail.

CONFIDENCE: 72
